messages:
maria_g: FYI security scan + CI smoke both flagged a few things after yesterday's dep bump. Tokenizers wheel failing on manylinux build and transforms tests failing on macOS wheel. Also noticed KMS permission errors when running bootstrapping in private builds.

benji: Ugh. Which CVE IDs are we seeing? Is tokenizers upstream or our vendored wheel?

maria_g: It's showing up as CVE-2024-25550 (tokenizers) in the scanner metadata. The pip install error is: `ERROR: Could not build wheels for tokenizers, which is required to install pyproject.toml` in the macOS runners. CI log snippet:```Collecting tokenizers==0.14.3
  Building wheel for tokenizers (pyproject.toml) ... error
  OSError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'manylinux2014'```

sophie: The KMS perms are separate but surfaced same pipeline run? What scope error do you see?

maria_g: KMS failure is `AccessDeniedException: kms:Encrypt` when the private job tries to encrypt the ephemeral key during worker boot. Looks like a role change in staging IAM. So two parallel issues: dep CVE + wheel build + KMS policy drift.

benji: For the tokenizers CVE we should follow triage: reproduce locally, check upstream patch, and see if a backport exists. If wheel build is failing on manylinux, short-term we can avoid building wheels in CI by installing the sdist or pinning a previously built wheel.

maria_g: Reproduction notes I ran: `python -m pip wheel tokenizers==0.14.3 -v` -> same error. Upstream issue mentions manylinux tag churn. No fixed release yet (open PR).

security-bot: Vulnerability CVE-2024-25550 assigned severity: HIGH. Suggested action: pin older non-vulnerable minor if compatible, or apply upstream patch and run regression evals.

sophie: We should not pin to an older version unless it is confirmed safe. Suggest a two-track plan: 1) temporary CI hotpatch to skip wheel build by using manylinux prebuilt wheel from our internal cache (or pip --no-build-isolation install from binary wheel). 2) create a poetry.lock rollback branch that pins tokenizers to last-known-good SHA and run full canary evaluation.

benji: Agreed. I can open a PR that: - reverts the tokenizers bump in poetry.lock to previous resolution - adds a CI job step to fetch internal wheel cache blob if available - adds a gating smoke test that checks `pip wheel tokenizers` succeeds on macOS runner.

maria_g: Also we need an action on the KMS drift: I can open a Jira to revert the recent role change or add `kms:Encrypt` to the worker role for staging; will coordinate with infra. That will unstick the private build bootstraps.

benji: Timeline: I'll aim to get the poetry.lock rollback PR up within 2 hours, include a short changelog and reason. Canary rollout to staging tomorrow AM after pytest/e2e.

sophie: For the security side I'll draft a short advisory and mark the CVE as under investigation. Also add a watch to the model-serving Dedicated pools since tokenizers used there for tokenization at serve-time.

maria_g: Notes for PR description (copy into PR): "hotpatch: temporary rollback of tokenizers dep due to wheel build break and active CVE-2024-25550; restores CI green while upstream patch is evaluated. Includes CI fallback to internal wheel cache and adds regression test for wheel build on macOS runners."

deploy-bot: Created branch `hotfix/tokenizers-rollback-1748204510` and triggered pipeline #4523.

benji: Pipeline failing on wheel step in macOS still, but the cache fallback picked up for linux. I'll ping infra to upload a built wheel for macOS to the cache.

maria_g: Follow-ups: - @sophie please file advisory and add affected services list - @benji attach the failing CI logs to the PR - @infra (I'll DM) for KMS role revert - set eviction to canary for Dedicated tokenizers nodes if we see degraded performance

sophie: Done — advisory created (SEC-2024-045) and linked to the ticket. Services tagged: inference-api, batch-embeddings, local-dev.

benji: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1923 with rollback + CI fallback. Adding reviewers: @maria_g @sophie @eng-oncall.

maria_g: Thanks. If upstream releases a patch we'll prepare a follow-up PR to bump and run the full quality eval suite. For now marking priority: P1 (CI outage + CVE).

security-bot: Label update: severity=HIGH, status=triage-in-progress, owner=benji."
